questions.text: What does the income statement principally summarize?

options.a: Assets and liabilities at one date only
options.b: Changes in shares outstanding exclusively
options.c: Revenues, expenses, gains, and losses recognized during a period
options.d: Cash financing inflows exclusively

questions.text: Why can net income differ from cash generated in the same period?

options.a: Every accounting expense is paid immediately
options.b: Accrual accounting recognizes some revenues and expenses before or after related cash flows
options.c: All financial statements use exclusively cash accounting
options.d: Cash revenue is never recognized as income

questions.text: Under the general revenue-recognition principle, when is revenue recognized?

options.a: When the customer obtains control of the promised good or service
options.b: Whenever inventory is produced
options.c: Immediately when a prospective customer requests a quote
options.d: Only when the customer transfers cash

questions.text: What does recognizing a credit sale typically create?

options.a: A liability and a dividend
options.b: A reduction in cash and sales
options.c: Revenue and accounts receivable
options.d: Only financing cash inflow

questions.text: Which is the first step of the IFRS 15 revenue-recognition model?

options.a: Recognize net income before performance
options.b: Calculate the firm's cost of capital
options.c: Recognize all revenue on the signing date
options.d: Identify the contract with the customer

questions.text: What is a performance obligation?

options.a: A promise by shareholders to repurchase shares
options.b: A contractual promise to transfer a distinct good or service to the customer
options.c: A bank covenant requiring interest payment
options.d: A commitment to distribute all net income

questions.text: Why must a company identify multiple performance obligations within a single contract?

options.a: Every contract necessarily has one obligation
options.b: Every obligation must be reported as a separate company
options.c: The contract must be treated entirely as financing
options.d: Revenue may need to be allocated and recognized separately for distinct promised goods or services

questions.text: What is the third step in the five-step model?

options.a: Choose the firm's share price
options.b: Record all cash as operating profit
options.c: Determine the transaction price
options.d: Classify the acquisition as goodwill

questions.text: How is a transaction price allocated among separate obligations?

options.a: Using relative standalone selling prices or reasonable estimates
options.b: Only to the least profitable obligation
options.c: By the order goods are listed in the contract
options.d: Equally in all cases regardless of value

questions.text: What is the final step of the five-step model?

options.a: Pay all suppliers before recognizing sales
options.b: Recognize revenue as or when each performance obligation is satisfied
options.c: Write off all inventory before delivering it
options.d: Record a receivable when management approves the budget

questions.text: When is revenue recognized for a service obligation satisfied continuously over time?

options.a: Over time as performance is delivered
options.b: All at contract inception regardless of work completed
options.c: Only when the final invoice is sent in all cases
options.d: Only when the firm's annual accounts are audited

questions.text: What is the main analytical benefit of segment reporting?

options.a: Guaranteeing consistent margins across business units
options.b: Disaggregating revenue and performance by product, business, or geographical area
options.c: Eliminating all transfer-pricing issues
options.d: Making consolidated financial statements unnecessary

questions.text: Which pattern may be hidden by stable consolidated revenue?

options.a: Total absence of currency effects
options.b: All business units changing at identical rates
options.c: One business segment shrinking while another grows
options.d: An unchanging geographic sales mix

questions.text: What is cost of goods sold (COGS)?

options.a: All capital raised through borrowing
options.b: Cost attributable to goods sold during the reporting period
options.c: Market value of unsold inventory only
options.d: Dividends declared on ordinary shares

questions.text: What does gross profit equal?

options.a: Assets minus liabilities
options.b: Net income less dividends
options.c: Operating cash flow plus financing cash flow
options.d: Sales revenue less cost of goods sold

questions.text: Which costs are typically included in selling, general, and administrative expenses?

options.a: Sales staff, marketing, and administrative overhead
options.b: Purchase price of all inventory remaining unsold
options.c: Dividends declared to shareholders
options.d: Repayment of bond principal

questions.text: What is a restructuring charge?

options.a: An expense resulting from changes such as reorganization or downsizing
options.b: Cash received from ordinary share issuance
options.c: The periodic coupon paid to bondholders by definition
options.d: A mandatory asset revaluation gain

questions.text: How does common-size income-statement analysis typically scale each line item?

options.a: By total debt only
options.b: By total sales or revenue
options.c: By the share price
options.d: By total number of employees exclusively

questions.text: Why can comparisons of SG&A-to-sales across firms be misleading?

options.a: SG&A includes only interest expense
options.b: Every firm has identical administrative needs
options.c: SG&A is legally fixed as a percentage of sales
options.d: Different business models and expense classifications affect the ratio

questions.text: Under IAS 38, how are research expenditures ordinarily treated?

options.a: Recorded directly as contributed equity
options.b: Always recognized as goodwill
options.c: Expensed when incurred
options.d: Always capitalized with an unlimited useful life

questions.text: Under IAS 38, when may development expenditures be capitalized?

options.a: Never under any circumstances
options.b: Only once all development-related cash is recovered
options.c: When specified recognition criteria, including demonstrable technical feasibility and future benefits, are met
options.d: Whenever management hopes that a product will succeed

questions.text: Why might high reported R&D expense not imply weak innovation prospects?

options.a: Research expenses are dividends to shareholders
options.b: Research investment can create future potential even when its costs are expensed today
options.c: R&D can never affect future cash flows
options.d: Every research project produces immediate revenue

questions.text: Which comparison is especially helpful when assessing R&D spending?

options.a: R&D relative to employee ages
options.b: R&D against the previous day's share price
options.c: R&D divided only by bond face value
options.d: R&D as a share of revenue across time and against suitable peers

questions.text: Why should analysts examine the commercial pipeline alongside R&D spending?

options.a: Spending alone does not reveal whether research is likely to yield viable products
options.b: A pipeline is reported as cash equivalents
options.c: All R&D amounts are capitalized regardless of results
options.d: The number of research projects is irrelevant to future profits

questions.text: What is depreciation?

options.a: The amortization of common share capital
options.b: Systematic allocation of a tangible depreciable asset's cost over its useful life
options.c: An automatic increase in the market price of PPE
options.d: Cash paid each month to buy replacement equipment

questions.text: What is amortization?

options.a: The revaluation of every indefinite-lived brand
options.b: The reduction of bond principal in all circumstances
options.c: Cash received from dividends
options.d: Systematic expense allocation for finite-lived intangible assets

questions.text: Why may depreciation expense change without a matching immediate cash outflow?

options.a: The expense is a new ordinary share issue
options.b: Depreciation creates cash from customers
options.c: It allocates past capitalized costs to current-period earnings
options.d: All assets are purchased on the depreciation date

questions.text: How can depreciation analysis provide insight into future operations?

options.a: It determines the market value of every bond
options.b: It sets the future selling price of products
options.c: It identifies the number of all future customers with certainty
options.d: It helps assess asset use, replacement requirements, and the age of productive capacity

questions.text: What is a discontinued operation?

options.a: Any operating cost below budget
options.b: Any customer contract that was not renewed
options.c: A disposed or held-for-sale component meeting the relevant separation criteria
options.d: A temporary fall in one product's selling price

questions.text: Why are results of discontinued operations separated from continuing operations?

options.a: To ensure discontinued operations never affect net income
options.b: To eliminate the need for comparatives
options.c: To help users assess the performance likely to persist in the remaining business
options.d: To classify all divestitures as inventory

questions.text: What is basic earnings per share (EPS)?

options.a: Cash flow divided by accounts payable
options.b: Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by weighted-average ordinary shares outstanding
options.c: Net income divided by closing debt
options.d: Revenue divided by total assets

questions.text: Why use weighted-average shares rather than simply year-end shares for EPS?

options.a: The share count may change during the year
options.b: Closing shares always equal weighted-average shares
options.c: Weighted-average shares exclude shares issued for cash
options.d: A firm must keep its share count constant

questions.text: What causes dilution in the EPS context?

options.a: The firm holds more cash equivalents
options.b: Interest expense always decreases
options.c: Expenses are replaced with cash inflows
options.d: Potential ordinary shares can increase the share count, reducing per-share earnings

questions.text: Which security may give rise to diluted EPS calculations?

options.a: An ordinary rent prepayment
options.b: A fixed-asset purchase order
options.c: A convertible bond
options.d: A supplier invoice with no conversion feature

questions.text: What is the general relationship between basic and diluted EPS for profitable firms with dilutive instruments?

options.a: Diluted EPS is always much greater than basic EPS
options.b: They must differ even without potential shares
options.c: Basic EPS equals market price per share
options.d: Diluted EPS is no greater than basic EPS

questions.text: Why might employee stock options dilute existing shareholders?

options.a: Exercise can increase shares outstanding at favorable prices for option holders
options.b: Options do not affect ownership percentages
options.c: Options guarantee higher cash flow per share
options.d: Exercise always reduces the number of shares outstanding

questions.text: What is comprehensive income?

options.a: Net income plus other comprehensive income
options.b: Cash from operations plus cash from investing
options.c: Dividends plus share repurchases
options.d: Sales minus total assets

questions.text: Which item is a typical example of other comprehensive income under relevant IFRS rules?

options.a: Certain foreign currency translation differences
options.b: Routine wages paid to employees
options.c: Cost of inventory sold
options.d: Ordinary sales revenue from customers

questions.text: Why may some unrealized gains and losses appear in OCI instead of profit or loss?

options.a: Every market value movement must be operating revenue
options.b: Relevant standards require or allow separate treatment outside current net income
options.c: All unrealized gains must always be paid out immediately
options.d: OCI is the same as bank cash

questions.text: Which statement is correct about OCI and equity?

options.a: OCI can never change book equity
options.b: OCI is always a trade liability
options.c: OCI generally affects accumulated comprehensive income within equity
options.d: OCI must equal dividends paid

questions.text: What is a reclassification adjustment for OCI?

options.a: A transfer of certain previously recognized OCI amounts into profit or loss when required
options.b: An adjustment that changes sales into cash
options.c: A reclassification of receivables as inventories
options.d: A conversion of all loans into equity

questions.text: Why do analysts review both net income and total comprehensive income?

options.a: Comprehensive income never contains any information beyond cash flow
options.b: Net income includes all changes in market capitalization
options.c: OCI cannot be material
options.d: Some economically important gains and losses are excluded from net income

questions.text: What is the main distinction between profit and cash flow for a credit sale?

options.a: Both are always recorded only on payment
options.b: Revenue can be recognized before the associated cash is collected
options.c: The cash flow must occur before a legal sale
options.d: A credit sale cannot affect current-period income

questions.text: What happens to the financial statements when revenue is recognized for an advance payment already received?

options.a: Cash must rise again by the same amount
options.b: The firm records a new loan
options.c: An intangible asset is always impaired
options.d: Deferred revenue falls and income rises, without new cash necessarily being received then

questions.text: Why is one-off restructuring expense not necessarily a good predictor of future operating profit?

options.a: It may be transitory rather than recurring
options.b: It must recur at the same amount every year
options.c: It is always shown as a dividend
options.d: It is identical to revenue from continuing operations

questions.text: What is a risk when management reduces R&D spending to lift current profit?

options.a: Future competitive strength must increase
options.b: Current earnings may improve at the expense of future innovation and cash-generating capacity
options.c: All research expenses become balance-sheet assets
options.d: No accounting or economic effect occurs

questions.text: What does the net profit margin express?

options.a: Total assets divided by sales
options.b: Operating cash flow relative to current debt
options.c: Net income relative to revenue
options.d: Dividend payout per new share issue

questions.text: What does gross margin deterioration potentially indicate?

options.a: Guaranteed increase in future equity returns
options.b: Higher production costs, weaker pricing power, or adverse sales mix
options.c: Elimination of competition
options.d: Automatic improvement in operating efficiency

questions.text: Why is operating profit often more informative about ongoing business activities than an isolated disposal gain?

options.a: Operating profit better reflects recurring activities when non-recurring items are separated
options.b: Disposal gains are guaranteed to repeat yearly
options.c: Only disposal gains affect enterprise value
options.d: Operating profit is identical to cash from financing

questions.text: Why can a company report positive net income even with negative operating cash flow?

options.a: Positive net income legally requires positive operating cash flow
options.b: Net income is defined as bank deposits
options.c: Accrual revenues and working-capital changes can separate earnings from cash generation
options.d: Operating cash flow excludes customer receipts

questions.text: Why must share-based compensation be considered when assessing EPS and shareholder value?

options.a: Share awards are an item of investing cash inflow
options.b: Share awards create compensation costs and may alter shares outstanding
options.c: Share awards never have an economic cost
options.d: Share awards guarantee a higher share price

questions.text: What is the purpose of earnings per share as a standardized measure?

options.a: To replace the need for analyzing a firm's revenue mix
options.b: To measure the exact market value per share
options.c: To measure bondholders' coupon yield
options.d: To scale attributable earnings by the weighted ownership unit for ordinary shareholders

questions.text: What is a drawback of interpreting EPS growth without examining share repurchases?

options.a: A falling share count can raise EPS without equivalent growth in total net income
options.b: Share repurchases are treated as income statement revenue
options.c: Share repurchases always increase total sales
options.d: EPS is mathematically unaffected by changes in the number of shares

questions.text: A manufacturer delivers goods on credit on 28 December and collects payment in January. When is revenue normally recognized if control transferred on 28 December?

options.a: Half in December and half in January by default
options.b: Only after the auditor signs the annual report
options.c: In December, with an accounts receivable until collection
options.d: In January only because cash is required

questions.text: A contract bundles a device and a separate two-year maintenance service. Which revenue-recognition approach best applies?

options.a: Recognize all revenue when the customer first pays regardless of delivery
options.b: Recognize no revenue until two years after the contract ends
options.c: Recognize all maintenance revenue when the device is manufactured
options.d: Identify distinct obligations, allocate the price, and recognize each when or as satisfied

questions.text: A firm capitalizes qualifying development costs rather than expensing them immediately. What is the typical initial effect, compared with expensing?

options.a: Lower current profit and lower assets in all periods
options.b: Higher current profit and higher recognized assets, followed by amortization or impairment as appropriate
options.c: No change in reported profit or assets
options.d: An automatic cash inflow from financing activities

questions.text: A firm reports rising EPS while aggregate net income is nearly unchanged. Which factor deserves particular investigation?

options.a: A higher number of shares issued without earnings growth
options.b: A change in the supplier payment period only
options.c: Share repurchases reducing the weighted-average share count
options.d: An increase in current assets

questions.text: A firm disposes of an operating component that qualifies as a discontinued operation. Which presentation best assists forecasting?

options.a: Separate the qualifying discontinued results from continuing operations
options.b: Treat all divested operations as OCI
options.c: Exclude the business's historical results from every report
options.d: Combine disposal proceeds directly with continuing revenue

questions.text: A company records a substantial foreign currency translation loss in OCI. What should an investor conclude?

options.a: The company's basic EPS must equal total comprehensive income per share
options.b: The company necessarily incurred an equal cash operating outflow
options.c: The loss must be included in cost of goods sold
options.d: Book equity and comprehensive income can be affected even though the amount is outside net income
